modelYear.note: Page is titled 'Tank 500 PHEV 2026'. This is the locally assembled car, booked from 26 Jan 2026 at PKR 22,500,000 ex-factory, the same price as the DB row.

bodyType.note: Headline: 'GWM Tank 500 HEV & PHEV Price – Pakistan's 1st Locally Assembled Full-Size SUV'.

driveType.note: Drive Train row: 'AWD'. The GWM Pakistan site (gwm-pakistan.com) also calls it 'Hi-4T Intelligent AWD Technology'.

groundClearanceMm.note: Ground Clearance row: '213 mm'. The HEV page gives 224 mm.

acChargingHours.note: 'Home Charge Time (0-100%): 7 Hours', with a 6.6 kW on-board charger.

dcChargingMinutes.note: 'Fast Charge Time (10-80% DC): 24 min'. This is the 10-80% window.

availability.value: Locally assembled (CKD) by Sazgar; bookings opened 26 Jan 2026 at PKR 22.5 million ex-factory, with delivery quoted at 3-4 months.
availability.note: The article states the ex-factory prices, that bookings open from 26 January, and a delivery time of 3 to 4 months.

distributor.note: The official GWM Pakistan site lists 'TANK 500 PHEV' at an ex-factory price of 22,500,000. The Tank 500 brochure footer reads 'Sazgar Engineering Works Limited ... gwm-pakistan.com'.

warranty.value: 6 years / 150,000 km standard warranty; powertrain (engine and transmission) 10 years / 1,000,000 km.
warranty.note: The official warranty page says: 'HAVAL offers a 6 year or 150,000km (whichever comes first) standard warranty for all of its vehicles... power-train (engine and transmission) warranty period is 10 years or 1,000,000km.' The PakWheels variant page adds a battery warranty of 8 years / 150,000 km.

conflicts.note: The PakWheels variant page says 'Seating Capacity: 5 persons', and the price-reveal article's table lists the PHEV as a 5-seater against the 7-seat HEV. Not from the distributor, so not corrected.

The variant page lists 'Pure Electric Range: 120 km' with no cycle named. A separate PakWheels article quotes '80-90 km real-world', which is the current DB span. Neither figure is from the distributor.
Not filled: the page's 'Kerb Weight 2850 KG' equals its wheelbase figure (2850 mm) and may be a copy error. International specs quoted by Gari.pk give 2,830 kg.

bodyType.note: Model page: body type SUV, 5 seats. The page covers the Tank 300 model generally and lists no hybrid variant.

driveType.note: Model page drive row: 4WD. This is model-level, not HEV-specific.

availability.value: Not officially launched in Pakistan: no Tank 300 HEV price or launch has been announced. GWM has brought a Tank 300 Hi4-T PHEV into the country for local testing.
availability.note: Gari.pk reports an Australian-spec Tank 300 Hi4-T PHEV in Pakistan for testing, with price and launch unconfirmed. The Tank 300 also does not appear in the model list on gwm-pakistan.com.

conflicts.note: The Tank 500 HEV feature tiles on the official GWM Pakistan site read 'Performance: 648Nm Torque, 246HP'. PakWheels lists '342 HP (Combined)'. 246 hp is probably the engine alone (2.0 T, about 180 kW), so it was not used as a correction.

torque.note: Sazgar Engineering Works Jolion brochure spec table, HEV column: DHT, FWD, Power KW (HP) 140 (190), Torque 375 NM. The gwm-pakistan.com Jolion tile also reads '375Nm Torque, 190HP'.

bodyType.note: The official GWM Pakistan site lists 'Haval Jolion' in category 'SUV'.

driveType.note: Sazgar brochure, Driveline row: FWD for both the 1.5T and the HEV (DHT). PakWheels HEV page: 'Drive Train FWD'.

lengthMm.note: Length row: '4475 mm'. The Sazgar brochure drawing shows both 4472 mm and 4475 mm.

widthMm.note: Brochure dimension drawing: 1841 mm. PakWheels HEV page gives the same.

heightMm.note: Brochure dimension drawing: 1619 mm. PakWheels HEV page gives the same.

availability.value: Locally assembled (CKD) by Sazgar; PakWheels lists it at PKR 9,116,216 ex-factory as the top Jolion variant.
availability.note: The variants table lists 'Haval Jolion HEV (Top of the line) 9,116,216' ex-factory. Local assembly is per https://www.pakwheels.com/blog/locally-assembled-haval-jolion-hev-specs-features/.

distributor.note: Brochure: 'This brochure is published by Sazgar Engineering Works Limited'. haval.pk now redirects to gwm-pakistan.com.

warranty.value: 6 years / 150,000 km standard warranty; powertrain 10 years / 1,000,000 km; hybrid battery, motor and controller 8 years / 160,000 km.
warranty.note: Official warranty page: 6 yr/150,000 km standard for all vehicles, engine and transmission 10 yr/1,000,000 km, and 'For the HEV variant, the battery, motor, and controller comes with an 8 year or 160,000km warranty.' The Sazgar Jolion brochure warranty box gives the same three figures.

power.note: The Sazgar (Pakistan distributor) brochure gives the HEV system output as 'Power KW (HP) 140 (190)', and gwm-pakistan.com says '190HP'. The DB's 187 is a kW-to-hp conversion of 140 kW rather than the published figure.

conflicts.note: PakWheels lists PKR 9,116,216 ex-factory. The DB price is marked indicative. priceMax and priceDisplay would change with it.
Not filled: PakWheels HEV page says 390 L, but the Sazgar brochure (covering both variants) says 'Storage Space capacity: 337L'.

acChargingHours.note: Pakistan launch article: 'Full AC charging takes around three hours.' PakWheels variant page: 'Home Charge Time (0-100%) 3 Hours'.

dcChargingMinutes.note: 'supports DC fast charging from 30% to 80% in under 28 minutes' (30-80% window). PakWheels labels the same 28 min as 10-80%.

warranty.value: 6 years / 150,000 km standard warranty; powertrain (engine and transmission) 10 years / 1,000,000 km.
warranty.note: The DB says 'Not confirmed'. The official GWM Pakistan warranty page states 6 yr/150,000 km standard 'for all of its vehicles' and 10 yr/1,000,000 km powertrain. PakWheels lists the PHEV battery warranty as 8 years / 160,000 km.

conflicts.note: The PakWheels variant page gives the charge port as 'CCS2', and the DB has a DC rate (34 kW), which implies a DC port.
Not filled: the same sentence gives an implausible '67 kWh' capacity (DB has 19.09 kWh), so the article's battery details are not reliable.

dcChargingMinutes.note: Australian review of the same 35.4 kWh / 321 kW car: 'a 30 to 80 per cent charge in 26 minutes' at 48 kW (30-80% window). The GWM AU/NZ pages say charge times assume a 48 kW DC charger. No Pakistani source gives a time.

acChargingHours.note: 'from 0 to 100 per cent in six hours' on a 6.6 kW wall charger. Australian-market, same battery and charger rating as the Pakistani car (ProPakistani: 35.43 kWh, 6.6 kW AC).

conflicts.note: The official page says the 6 yr/150,000 km standard warranty applies 'for all of its vehicles' but does not name the H6 GT specifically, so it is not used as a correction.

acceleration.note: Pakistan launch article (company figures): 'capable of going from 0 to 100 kilometers in around 7.5 seconds.' Same 240 hp / 530 Nm FWD DHT drivetrain as the DB row. A PakWheels review measured about 8 s.

warranty.note: The DB says 'Not confirmed'. The official GWM Pakistan warranty page states these terms for all vehicles, plus the HEV battery/motor/controller term. PakWheels' H6 HEV page also lists the battery at 8 years / 160,000 km.

The value is correct but not in the standard form ('FWD'). Formatting only.

dcChargingMinutes.note: ORA 03 400-Pro (the Pakistani variant) page: 'Fast Charge Time (10-80% DC): 41 min' (10-80% window).

conflicts.note: The official page states a 6 yr/150,000 km standard warranty 'for all of its vehicles'. The ORA 03 is no longer in the official line-up, so its terms at sale may differ. The PakWheels 400-Pro page gives the battery as 8 years / 150,000 km.
The variant page lists an electric range of 310 km with no cycle (the field shows '-'). This is already discussed in the DB notes (310 km WLTP vs 400 km CLTC).

groundClearanceMm.note: Australian spec page for the 58.3 kWh / 150 kW ORA 5 (the same battery and motor as the Pakistani car): 'Ground clearance 175mm'. CarExpert NZ also gives 175 mm. No Pakistani source states it.

dcChargingMinutes.note: '30 min' for '10-80 per cent' at 120 kW max DC (10-80% window). Australian 58.3 kWh car, the same pack as Pakistan's 58.33 kWh.
